Looking at this question, I need to consider the F200Y mutation in fungal β-tubulin and its effect on thiabendazole binding.

Thiabendazole is a benzimidazole anti-fungal drug that binds specifically to β-tubulin. The binding site involves specific amino acid residues that create the appropriate chemical environment for drug interaction.

The F200Y mutation substitutes phenylalanine (a non-polar aromatic amino acid) with tyrosine (a polar aromatic amino acid with an additional hydroxyl group). While this appears to be a conservative substitution (both are aromatic), the addition of the hydroxyl group at position 200 alters the local chemical environment of the binding pocket.

In studies of benzimidazole-tubulin interactions, this particular mutation at position 200 has been shown to disrupt the specific binding interactions required for thiabendazole to properly dock into the β-tubulin binding site, leading to reduced drug affinity and resistance.

[ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
